players.product: Large-scale water treatment systems for semiconductor makers, plus maintenance, consumables and piping materials for semiconductor manufacturing equipment

quarterly_data.quarter: Nomura Micro Science annual securities report: FY2026 (06-23-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Fiscal year ended March 31, 2026 (annual securities report): orders received JPY 47,694 million (-49.5% YoY), net sales JPY 56,245 million (-41.6%), operating profit JPY 6,667 million (-56.6%), ordinary profit JPY 5,629 million (-58.0%), net profit attributable to owners of the parent JPY 3,818 million (-62.6%). Water treatment systems sales JPY 36,723 million (-53.4%) on the reaction to the prior year's large water treatment projects and delays in the construction start of some large projects already ordered; maintenance and consumables JPY 18,626 million (+19.9%) as orders stayed firm, mainly from semiconductor-related companies; other businesses JPY 895 million (-56.5%) as sales of piping materials for large semiconductor manufacturing equipment ran their course. Management states profits fell at every level because the large US water treatment projects ran their course and some ordered large projects started construction late.
quarterly_data.figure: Net sales JPY 56,245 million (-41.6%); operating profit JPY 6,667 million (-56.6%); orders JPY 47,694 million (-49.5%)

quarterly_data.quarter: Nomura Micro Science annual securities report: FY2026 (06-23-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Segments, year to March 2026 (annual securities report): Japan sales JPY 25,768 million (-2.8%), operating profit JPY 3,083 million (-23.1%), as large water treatment projects progressed smoothly but the prior year had some high-margin large projects; Korea JPY 9,158 million (+184.1%), operating profit JPY 402 million (+25.7%), on smooth progress of large water treatment projects ordered the prior year; China JPY 7,687 million (-22.7%), operating profit JPY 94 million (-90.5%), as semiconductor capex paused and orders were weak; Taiwan JPY 3,535 million (-17.6%), operating profit JPY 754 million (-51.4%), as maintenance and consumables orders were firm but construction of a large water treatment system started late; US JPY 10,078 million (-80.8%), operating profit JPY 2,355 million (-72.3%), on the reaction to large water treatment projects of prior years; Other (Singapore subsidiary, set up to follow the dispersion of semiconductor production sites, began operating in the first quarter) sales JPY 16 million from maintenance and consumables, operating loss JPY 21 million. The company states its overseas sales ratio is about 70%.
quarterly_data.figure: Japan JPY 25,768 million (-2.8%); Korea JPY 9,158 million (+184.1%); US JPY 10,078 million (-80.8%); overseas sales ratio about 70%

quarterly_data.quarter: Nomura Micro Science annual securities report: FY2026 (06-23-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Orders and order backlog, year to March 2026 (annual securities report): water treatment systems business orders received JPY 46,799,154 thousand (50.6% of the prior year) and order backlog at year-end JPY 32,219,174 thousand (79.0% of the prior year); other businesses orders JPY 895,116 thousand (43.5% of the prior year). Management states capex by semiconductor-related companies, its main customers, remains strong, and the drop in orders reflects the reaction to the prior year's large water treatment project orders. The company has no production results: installation of the ultrapure water and wastewater treatment systems it is ordered is fully outsourced to partner construction companies.
quarterly_data.figure: Order backlog JPY 32,219,174 thousand (79.0% of prior year); water treatment orders JPY 46,799,154 thousand (50.6% of prior year)

quarterly_data.quarter: Nomura Micro Science annual securities report: FY2026 (06-23-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Medium-term plan TTT-26 (Together Toward Transformation-26), drawn up in 2023 (annual securities report): the company aims for management targets for the plan's fiscal 2026 (the year beginning April 2026, i.e. to March 2027) of net sales JPY 1,010 hundred million, operating profit JPY 146 hundred million, ROE of 25% or more and ROIC of 22% or more, with the vision of becoming an outstanding maker of ultrapure water systems for semiconductor and pharmaceutical plants, centred on Asia. Measures: stronger sales, reform of the engineering process (prefabricated construction that turns delivered systems into units and skids, with partner companies, for efficiency, more capacity, shorter delivery and less on-site work), accelerating the 'SMART UP 3' R&D programme, human capital and environmental work. Management states semiconductor production sites, including those of its important customers, are spreading from East Asia to the rest of the world, so it is strengthening its US subsidiary and has set up a Singapore subsidiary that has started sales to target Southeast Asia, where continued semiconductor investment is expected; in pharmaceuticals it placed a sales office in the Hokuriku region and is also pursuing projects in Korea and the US.
quarterly_data.figure: Targets for the year to March 2027 (plan fiscal 2026): net sales JPY 1,010 hundred million; operating profit JPY 146 hundred million; ROE 25% or more; ROIC 22% or more

quarterly_data.quarter: Nomura Micro Science annual securities report: FY2026 (06-23-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: R&D, year to March 2026 (annual securities report): R&D expenses JPY 493 million with 46 R&D staff at year-end, centred on the water treatment systems business. Management states it works to raise three things - ultrapure water purity, analytical sensitivity and environmental contribution - to supply the water quality leading-edge semiconductor manufacturing requires, and is also developing functional-water systems (ozone water, hydrogen water) built on its ultrapure water technology. Last year it built a new development building to develop ultrapure water systems for next-generation semiconductors, and it plans to build an analysis building for high-precision analysis technology and research into the causes of impurities. It developed what it calls the world's first monitor able to detect the bacterial toxin endotoxin rapidly and continuously, now in demonstration tests, to open up the water-for-injection market. Its Korean subsidiary has an R&D function close to major overseas users.

quarterly_data.quarter: Nomura Micro Science annual securities report: FY2026 (06-23-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Capital expenditure (annual securities report): capex totalled JPY 1,419 million in the year to March 2026, mainly for equipment renewal, chiefly an R&D center built in the Japan segment for JPY 849 million; leased assets, used mainly to provide services to customers, are excluded. The company sometimes meets customers' wish to cut their capex through BOOM (Build Own Operate and Maintenance) contracts, under which it owns and operates the ultrapure water system and the customer pays a usage fee for the ultrapure water it uses. At year-end there were no plans for significant new facilities or disposals.
quarterly_data.figure: Capex JPY 1,419 million; R&D center JPY 849 million
